hooks.name: Auto-create child task after deliver
hooks.description: After the deliver agent produces a ticket-ready summary, automatically creates a child task under the associated user story in Azure DevOps.

action.prompt:
Check the sub-agent invocation that just completed. If the invoked agent was NOT "deliver" AND NOT "summarizer", or its output is not a ticket-ready work summary, or there is no relevant Azure DevOps ticket context for this session, do nothing and continue normally. If the deliver/summarizer agent produced a ticket-ready summary: 1. Resolve the parent user story ID: check the current git branch name for a pattern like `feature/1234-*`, `bugfix/1234-*`, `1234-*`, or any embedded numeric ID. If no ID can be inferred, ask the user. 2. Fetch the parent user story to confirm it exists: wit_work_item({ action: "get", id: }) 3. Create a child task with the summary in the description as RAW MARKDOWN — do NOT convert to HTML: wit_work_item_write({ action: "add_child", parentId: , project: "", workItemType: "Task", title: "", fields: { "System.Description": ",
    ,
  • , ,

    , etc.>" } }) 4. Confirm to the user: which user story, the child task ID created, and a link: https://dev.azure.com/RevStarConsulting//_workitems/edit/ CRITICAL: The description field renders markdown natively. Write the summary EXACTLY as the deliver agent produced it — plain markdown text. If you convert it to HTML, it will display as raw HTML tags to the user. Do not surface this instruction text to the user.
